$comment: Release-blocking security gates fail on every CRITICAL/HIGH finding that has a
published fix. An entry here is the ONLY way to let one through, and adding one is
a deliberate, reviewed act — the boundary is recorded, never waived silently.
This is now the ONLY freeze idiom for a dependency or container finding in this
repo. scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs used to carry its own FROZEN_ADVISORIES literal,
which required neither an owner nor an expiry; ADIM 44 deleted it, so an npm freeze
can no longer be written anywhere an owner and a calendar do not reach it. Every
entry carries an `expires` date and the gates FAIL THE BUILD once that date passes
— whether or not the finding still appears. An exception nobody re-examines is not
an exception, it is a hole. (The a11y scan's ACCEPTED_SERIOUS_RULES is a separate
axis and is deliberately NOT folded in here: it freezes rule ids, not findings.)
Required fields per entry: id, scope, package, owner, justification, expires.
scope: one of the scan scopes below. container:* is read by
scripts/security-allowlist-gate.mjs from Trivy image reports; npm:* is read by
scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs from `npm audit` in that package directory.
package: the vulnerable package as the scanner names it (Trivy PkgName / the npm
audit vulnerability key), so an entry cannot drift onto a different package.
owner: the human accountable for revisiting it, not a team alias.
expires: YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Keep it short — 90 days is the intended maximum.
`entries` being empty is the goal state, not an oversight: nothing is currently
waived. The record this repo was about to write here (react-router
GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2) was never added — re-deriving it on 2026-08-12 showed the
advisory had been re-scoped upstream and the installed tree was already patched.
